ashby:aerovect:ad44b8f8-699a-460d-bb0d-9.summary:
AeroVect is transforming ground handling with autonomy, redefining how airlines and ground service providers around the globe run day-to-day operations. We are a Series A company backed by top-tier venture capital investors in aviation and autonomous driving. Our customers include some of the world’s largest airlines and ground handling providers. For more information, visit www.aerovect.com .

The Staff PMT is responsible for defining the strategy, roadmap, and product requirements for AeroVect’s Autonomous Ground Support Equipment (AGSE) Service, which will redefine how flagship airlines and airport customers around the globe run day-to-day operations. This role will ensure that the AGSE Service is capable, performant, and reliable enough to support the needs of AeroVect’s customers.

sections.title: Who We Are
paras: Working with the Director of Safety, Systems, and Product, the PMT sets the direction for the product organization at AeroVect, with a purview spanning autonomous driving capabilities, fleet operations, and evaluation infrastructure. The PMT will be responsible for ensuring that every product decision for the AGSE Service is anchored in customer needs and commercial reality. They will directly engage with airline and airport customers to understand their needs, translate them into product requirements, and incorporate them into a product roadmap supporting multiple customers and business objectives.

As Staff PMT, you will lead a team of PMTs in defining and owning the roadmap for each product vertical, providing the clarity and structure needed to translate high-level service goals into executable system-level plans. As a product leader, they will mentor other PMTs to grow their product skills by establishing best practices for autonomy product development - including how the team defines requirements, measures capability progress, and makes data-driven decisions.

This role requires a unique blend of product leadership, technical depth, commercial fluency, and executive-level communication skills. The PMT must be a strong cross-functional leader that is capable of guiding engineering organizations through ambiguity and driving tradeoffs for a product that is both safety- and operation-critical.

sections.title: You Will
bullets:
Define and own the AGSE Service product strategy and roadmap

• Own the top-level product roadmap spanning autonomous driving capabilities, fleet operations, and evaluation infrastructure
Drive clarity on what the company is building, why, and by when to create alignment across commercial, engineering, and operations teams

Build the measurement foundation for continuous improvement

• Define KPIs across capability, performance, and reliability to track product health and drive prioritization
Partner with XFN teams to develop data collection and analysis pipelines that support development, V&V, and continuous improvement

Drive technical execution across a safety-critical autonomous system

• Partner with Systems Engineering to decompose product needs into system requirements, test plans, and acceptance criteria
Participate in system design discussions across Autonomy, Infrastructure, and Hardware - ensuring technical architectures serve product goals and operational realities
Work with Engineering leadership to make informed trade-off decisions that align with business goals and technical feasibility
Work with Program Management to ensure roadmap commitments are tracked, blockers are surfaced early, and dependencies are known

5+ years of Product Management experience owning multi-system, technically complex products end-to-end
Experience building and shipping products in environments where safety, reliability, and real-time performance are non-negotiable
Proven ability to ship 0 → 1 products in a fast-paced environment
Demonstrated experience engaging directly with enterprise or operational customers - conducting discovery, translating needs into requirements, and managing relationships
Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities, with a data-driven approach to decision-making
Track record of leading cross-functional teams and influencing without direct authority
Exceptional communication and stakeholder management skills with the ability to translate between technical depth and executive clarity

Patreon is a media and community platform where over 300,000 creators give their biggest fans access to exclusive work and experiences. We offer creators a variety of ways to engage with their fans and build a lasting business including: paid memberships, free memberships, community chats, live video, and selling to fans directly with one-time purchases.

sections.title: About the Team
paras: The IT team makes sure every Patreon employee has the tools they need to build and support our product. We sit alongside Workplace, People Operations, and Systems which gives us a view across every business function and the access to act on what we see. You’ll join a team that already administratively owns the AI stack, the identity and access layer, and the systems that connect them.

Our approach to AI at Patreon
At Patreon, we believe in the power of human creativity and see AI as a tool to support our teams, not replace the creators at the heart of our mission.
Learn more about Patreon's approach to AI from our CEO, Jack Conte .
bullets: Patreon does NOT use creator work to train generative AI models (i.e. LLMs or image generators) that allow other people to replicate your work.
We ARE actively fighting to protect creators from AI spam, and from having their work scraped without their consent.

We are NOT blanket-prohibiting work that was made with AI tools or AI assistance. While we’re incredibly frustrated that AI companies aren’t paying creators, there are clear examples of deeply creative people using these tools in a beautiful way for true self expression, and we do not want Patreon to stifle that.

Human creativity is not going anywhere. Humans will be making and enjoying art made by other humans for a long, long time. Our strategy and vision (and business success) actually depend on that. Patreon is going all in on the belief that humans love the creativity of other humans.

sections.title: About the Role
paras: Patreon runs on a modern AI stack (Claude, Zapier, Replit, Gemini, Databricks and more), and most of the company uses it daily. What we have not yet built is the connective tissue between the people who know their workflows best and the practices that turn those workflows into durable, governed tools.

This role owns that connection. You will work alongside teams across the company to redesign how work gets done, in two directions at once: building new workflows and tools with AI, and making existing workflows AI-enabled so that the systems people already rely on become faster and smarter. Some of that you will build yourself. Some of it will help enable non-eng teams to build. All of it you will ship with the same discipline necessary to maintain systems over time: version control, review, testing, staged rollout, monitoring and a clear ownership.

The scope is company-wide and the role is an individual contributor with real autonomy. You will set the roadmap, run intake, and be accountable for a portfolio of deliverables and the metrics behind them.

Co-own, with Engineering and Security, the standards for how AI-enabled workflows touch production data: data classification, read and write permissions, connector and agent approval, audit logging, retention, and what must never leave a governed environment
Help Engineering prioritize internal tooling work by bringing quantified business impact, clear scope and committed business owners to the table

sections.title: The Opportunity
paras: SandboxAQ’s AI Simulation (AISim) division develops and applies Large Quantitative Models (LQMs) that are grounded in physics, chemistry, mathematics and biology to simulate molecular behavior with scientific precision and accelerate discovery in the physical world across biopharma, chemicals, advanced materials, healthcare, and so much more.

Within AISim, ChemSim is SandboxAQ's AI-driven materials discovery platform. We are seeking an exceptional Product Manager to own the Catalysis vertical. This is a dual-mandate role. In the near term, you will be the product owner for catalysis within SandboxAQ's $500M CHIPS Act R&D award from the U.S. Department of Commerce, translating contractual objectives into product requirements and external fulfilment, whilst partnering with Program Managers to ensure successful milestone delivery. In parallel, you will build the commercial foundation that turns catalysis from a government-funded R&D workstream into a product-led business generating durable, recurring revenue from the broader materials and process-chemistry market.

Catalysis is one of the largest and most consequential application areas in applied chemistry. It underpins refining and downstream oil and gas, commodity and petrochemical production, emissions control, and the energy transition (hydrogen electrolysis, carbon utilization, e-fuels and chemical recycling etc) alongside semiconductor process chemistry and fine chemical synthesis. Across nearly all of these markets the bottleneck is the same: catalyst discovery and optimization remain slow, experimental and expensive, and the simulation tools available today answer narrower questions than the ones that actually decide a process. This is a once-in-a-career opportunity to shape a category-defining AI platform for materials science at the intersection of national security, scientific discovery, and commercial scale.

sections.title: Key Responsibilities
bullets: Own the end-to-end Catalysis product strategy, vision and roadmap, spanning CHIPS Act contractual deliverables, vertical scientific depth, and commercial expansion into new markets.
Translate the program's catalysis objectives into clear product requirements, a vertical roadmap, and the evidence packages required for Fulfillment Notices to the U.S. Department of Commerce.

Define the dataset and model requirements for the vertical, chemical coverage, fidelity, and the benchmarking that determines where simulation investment is directed in partnership with our scientific and ML teams.
Drive the roadmap from property and energetics prediction toward reaction-level modelling, so that predictions can be validated against a customer's own process rather than assessed in isolation.

Contribute to the catalysis commercial strategy with commercial leadership: customer segmentation, scope of offer, packaging, and pricing model across semiconductor, refining and petrochemical, emissions control and energy-transition customers.

Build, manage, and own strategic partner relationships at the product level: Work with fabs and equipment OEMs, precursor and specialty materials suppliers, refiners and chemical producers, catalyst manufacturers, national laboratories and validation partners, translating partner requirements into product features.

Define and track strategic product and commercial KPIs: Manage the metrics that matter most including, Model accuracy requirements, workflow adoption, customer segment expansion, and recurring revenue growth , and drive course corrections against OKRs.
Develop and defend build-vs-buy and build-vs-partner recommendations for domain-specific scientific engines, datasets and validation tooling.

sections.title: Essential Skills & Experience
bullets: 5+ years in product management, including ownership of a technically deep product sold to external customers. Must be able to operate in a product capacity within business models that are software and service oriented

Strong domain grounding in materials science, catalysis, chemistry, or chemical engineering. Enough knowledge to sufficiently and credibly engage computational scientists, experimental validation partners, and domain SMEs.

Track record shipping AI/ML-driven scientific or engineering software to external, paying or contracted users; and shipping products where the ICP was not clearly understood or demand generation and funnel was not already in place.
Experience contributing to scope of offer, packaging and pricing decisions for technical software, or clear evidence of the commercial instinct to do so.
Ability to engage both computational scientists and industrial, refining, chemical or equipment OEM partners, and to turn partner requirements into product requirements.
Ability to reason commercially across multiple end markets at once, sizing opportunities, comparing them on evidence, and sequencing entry rather than pursuing all of them simultaneously.
Comfort navigating deep ambiguity: translating unclear scientific and customer problems into structured roadmaps, success criteria, and measurable outcomes.
Has an ownership mindset, and a rigorous operational execution track record.

sections.title: Highly Desired Skills & Experience
bullets: Experience in one or more major catalysis end markets, refining and downstream, petrochemicals and commodity chemicals, emissions control, or energy-transition catalysis such as electrolysis, carbon utilization, e-fuels or chemical recycling.

Familiarity with computational chemistry workflows such as density functional theory (DFT), molecular dynamics, or microkinetic modelling, and the judgement to evaluate technical feasibility and roadmap trade-offs.
Semiconductor or electronic materials process chemistry experience (e.g. deposition, etch, wafer cleaning, gas abatement etc).
Familiarity with homogeneous or solution-phase catalysis alongside heterogeneous surface chemistry, and a view on where each approach applies.
Understanding of machine-learned interatomic potentials, spin polarization in transition-metal systems, and the evaluation of ML models against experimental or first-principles reference data.
Track record building product-led growth motions for technical or scientific software, including self-serve adoption and land-and-expand commercial models.
Prior product or business development engagement with catalyst manufacturers, chemical producers, refiners, or semiconductor ecosystem partners such as fabs, equipment OEMs and precursor suppliers.
Experience with multi-tenant SaaS, API governance, and enterprise security and compliance requirements.

ashby:socure:ef4ab7b8-0a33-4ceb-9438-06c.summary:
Socure is building the identity trust infrastructure for the digital economy — verifying 100% of good identities in real time and stopping fraud before it starts. The mission is big, the problems are complex, and the impact is felt by businesses, governments, and millions of people every day.

We hire people who want that level of responsibility. People who move fast, think critically, act like owners, and care deeply about solving customer problems with precision. If you want predictability or narrow scope, this won’t be your place. If you want to help build the future of identity with a team that holds a high bar for itself — keep reading.

sections.title: Why Socure?
paras: We are looking for a Senior Technical Product Manager to join our Digital Intelligence team and lead the evolution of our Device Recognition products. In this role, you will own the technology that recognizes devices across sessions, customers, and channels, and binds them to verified identity through Socure's Global Device ID and Identity Graph. You will define how we collect signals through our Web and Mobile SDKs, how we build durable device fingerprints across browsers, operating systems, and device types, and how recognition holds up as platforms tighten their privacy controls.

Reporting directly to the Head of Digital Intelligence Products, you will work at the intersection of device intelligence, data science, and massive-scale engineering. You won't just be writing tickets; you will be deep in the data, writing your own queries, building prototypes, and testing hypotheses before the team commits to building.

This role is open to current product managers and to experienced engineers who want to branch out into product. If you have built device fingerprinting or tracking technology, are comfortable debating methods and trade-offs with engineers & data scientists, and measure your work by outcomes, we want to hear from you.

sections.title: What You'll Do
bullets: Own the Device Recognition Roadmap: Drive the end-to-end product lifecycle for Device Recognition and the Global Device ID, improving recognition accuracy, persistence over time, and linking of devices across customers. You will own priorities, scope, and release trade-offs.

Define Signal Collection: Partner with Engineering to define, prioritize, and deliver signal collection across our Web, iOS, and Android SDKs. You will own the trade-offs between signal richness, SDK footprint, performance, and privacy on each platform.

Navigate Platform Nuances: Track and respond to changes across browsers, operating systems, and device types, including privacy features such as tracking prevention, storage partitioning, fingerprinting protections, and app tracking restrictions that affect recognition.
Get Your Hands Dirty: Write your own SQL, analyze signal stability and distributions, and build prototypes to validate ideas before engineering invests in them.

Data Science Partnership: Work hand-in-hand with Data Scientists on the matching and linking logic behind device recognition. Together with Data Science and Engineering, you will define acceptance criteria for recognition performance (e.g., match rate, false merge and false split rates) and track them in production.

Continuous Discovery & Experimentation: Utilize prototyping and experimentation to de-risk solutions before building. You will validate hypotheses about signal stability, spoofing, emulators, and anti-detect browsers through data analysis and pilot programs.
Customer Evaluation: Define how customers evaluate and calibrate Device Recognition, including POCs against competitors.

Cross-Suite Integration: Engage with internal product teams to ensure Device Recognition integrates seamlessly with Behavioral Analytics, the broader Digital Intelligence suite, and other Socure Products (RiskOS, Document Verification, etc…) to provide a unified risk score to our clients.

sections.title: What You Bring
bullets: Experience: 5+ years of Product Management or Software Engineering experience, with at least 2+ years in a highly technical domain (Device Intelligence, Fraud Prevention, Identity, Cybersecurity, or AdTech). Engineers moving into product are welcome; tell us about the products you shaped.

Device Fingerprinting & Tracking: Hands-on experience building or managing device fingerprinting, device recognition, or tracking technology. You understand how browser, hardware, and network attributes combine into a device identifier, and where each one breaks down.

SDK & Platform Depth: You understand data collection through JavaScript and native SDKs, and the nuances between web, iOS, and Android, as well as across browsers and device types. You know what changes when a user goes incognito, clears storage, updates an OS, or runs an emulator or anti-detect browser.

Hands-On Technical Fluency: You are proficient in SQL and comfortable performing your own data analysis to answer questions without waiting for an analyst. You can build working prototypes in Python or a similar language. You understand API design (REST/JSON) and the basics of machine learning pipelines.

Outcome Over Output: You are goal oriented and focus on moving business metrics (e.g., "Increase cross-customer device recognition by 20%") rather than just shipping features. You are familiar with setting and tracking KPIs like match rates, False Positive Rates, and Fraud Detection Rates.

Problem Solving: You can partner with engineering and data science to break down complex, ambiguous problems, like "how do we recognize a returning device after its browser storage has been cleared?", into shippable iterations.
AI Fluency: You use AI tools in your daily work, including data analysis with Data Science, prototyping, and reporting.
Communication: You communicate clearly and concisely, in writing and in person, with engineers, data scientists, customers, and executives.

sections.title: Bonus Points
bullets: Device-Focused Company Experience: Prior experience at iovation, Sardine, Fingerprint, ThreatMetrix, IPQS, or other device-focused companies.
Device Integrity & Attestation: Familiarity with hardware-backed and platform signals such as Apple App Attest, DeviceCheck, and Google Play Integrity.
Graph & Entity Resolution: Experience linking entities (devices, users, accounts) across large datasets, including identity graphs.
Regulatory Knowledge: Understanding of privacy landscapes regarding device data and tracking (GDPR, ePrivacy, CCPA) and how consent and retention requirements influence product architecture.
Network Intelligence: Experience with IP, proxy, VPN, and carrier signals and how they complement device recognition.

ashby:speak:88b810f3-aa10-4e9e-9dbc-163f.summary:
Learning a language can change a life by opening doors to new cultures, careers, and communities. Two billion people around the world are actively trying to learn a language, but the best way to learn (one-on-one tutoring) is hard to access at scale and hasn’t been meaningfully improved in decades. Speak is building a human-level, AI-powered tutor in your pocket: a conversation-first experience that lets learners actually speak, get instant feedback, and progress through carefully designed lessons. The result is a complete path from beginner to confident speaker across multiple languages.

Speak first launched in South Korea in 2019, where Speak has now become the number one language learning app, and we now serve learners across many markets and 15+ languages. Speak is one of the world’s leading AI companies, with over $150m raised in venture investment from OpenAI, Accel, Founders…

Speak already has a scaled consumer product and a hard mission: help people actually become fluent, not just feel productive in an app. The long-term vision is a superhuman tutor — a system that understands a learner's level, goals, mistakes, context, and next best step, then creates or recommends the right lesson, conversation, drill, assessment, or review at the right moment.

Right now, enabling new languages and creating new professional courses depend on manual production. This role exists to build the product system that scales at the speed of software, makes high-velocity content generation possible with real quality guarantees, human review workflows, and pedagogical integrity.

Partner closely with curriculum, AI, engineering, product, and learning teams

Build feedback loops from learner behavior (ratings, completion, complaints, expert review) back into generation quality
Design the end-to-end workflow that moves priority content from request → generated draft → human review → launch

greenhouse:baselayer:5469414008.summary:
Every business in America needs a bank account to exist. The system that decides whether they're real, who's behind them, and whether they're a risk, runs on infrastructure from the 1980s. We're rebuilding that layer from scratch.

Baselayer is the identity layer for institutions across the United States — the most complete business graph in America and every human tied to it. We fuse public records, IRS data, sanctions lists, web signals, and fraud telemetry from 2,200+ financial institutions into a single graph that resolves any business and the humans behind it in milliseconds. The legacy credit bureaus took 50 years to build something that gets 60% match rates. We've built something that gets 98% in under two years.

sections.title: ABOUT BASELAYER
paras: Today we're trusted by over 20% of financial institutions in America — including FIS, Rho, Socure and leading loan infrastructure providers. But the graph is becoming infrastructure for anyone who needs to know if a business is real and worth trusting: gig platforms, marketplaces, AI companies, and commerce infrastructure at scale.
Trust is the substrate of every financial transaction. We're rebuilding it.

sections.title: ABOUT THE TEAM
paras: We're solving real-time entity resolution at a scale no one else has cracked — fusing dozens of data sources into a single business identity graph and resolving any entity in milliseconds. It's a graph AI problem, a retrieval problem, and a fraud-modeling problem stacked on top of each other. The technical depth is real.

You'd be joining a small team where the data moat is defensible, the research problems are open, and the infrastructure you build becomes load-bearing for businesses. Ownership is real. Velocity is real. There's no layer of process between an idea and shipping it.

We're at an inflection point — the graph is built, the match rates speak for themselves, and the hardest problems are still ahead: graph embeddings, fraud propagation models across the business network, real-time traversal at sub-100ms latency, and expanding the identity layer beyond finance into every platform that needs to trust a business.

sections.title: ABOUT THE ROLE
paras: As Baselayer's first dedicated Sr. Product Manager, you'll report directly to our CTO and own the creation, design, and full scoping of new products that take Baselayer beyond financial institutions and into new verticals where business identity is broken. You'll define what we build, why we build it, and what "done" looks like. You won't be inheriting a roadmap. You'll be writing one.

This role is hands-on. You'll write the specs, draw the wireframes, partner with design, and sit in eng standups. You'll also own the existing product surface: setting priorities, sequencing the roadmap, and making the daily calls that keep engineering shipping the right things. New verticals are the headline, but the day-to-day is a mix of zero-to-one product definition and disciplined operating cadence on what's already in market.

sections.title: New Product Definition & Scoping
bullets: Lead the scoping of new products targeting verticals beyond financial institutions, from initial thesis through detailed product spec
Translate market opportunity into product requirements, including target user, core workflows, success metrics, and what's explicitly out of scope
Build the artifacts that align the company: PRDs, one-pagers, wireframes, decision logs, and launch criteria
Own the "what" and the "why" so eng and design can own the "how"

sections.title: ABOUT THE TEAM
paras: AI agents are starting to transact: opening accounts, buying services, moving money on behalf of the businesses and people behind them. Every one of those transactions has a counterparty asking the question banks have always asked: who am I dealing with, and can I trust them? Today's identity infrastructure wasn't built to answer it at agent speed.

The Agentic Economy team is extending Baselayer's business graph into the trust layer for agentic commerce: verifiable credentials that bind an agent to the verified business and human behind it, a registry counterparties can query in real time, and verification APIs that plug into the networks, platforms, and protocols where agent transactions happen.

We run like a startup inside a startup: a small senior team led by our GM of Agentic Economy, working directly with payment networks, banks, wallet providers, and agent platforms. The category is being defined right now; the standards, seats, and infrastructure decisions of the next 18 months will be consequential for a decade.

You’ll write the positioning, build the sales narrative, run the launches, and prove what’s working. You’ll partner closely with the founders, sales, and product to turn a differentiated platform into a category-defining story, and your words will show up in every deal cycle and every product release.

You will connect DoorDash’s order and logistics platform with the aircraft, autonomy stack, mission-planning services, UTM capabilities, fleet-management tools, and operator workflows that execute each delivery. You will define how an order moves from merchant readiness through dispatch, airspace validation, autonomous flight, delivery, and completion within the broader DoorDash marketplace, ensuring that new features align to DoorDash Air’s roadmap across teams while balancing execution timelines against technical debt.

You will lead product direction across autonomy, aviation software, services, hardware, systems engineering, flight operations, UTM, safety, regulatory, data, and DoorDash platform teams. You will work closely with the Head of UTM and senior Engineering and Operations leaders to establish the product roadmap, clarify system boundaries, make build-versus-partner decisions, and align technical investment with operational scale and unit economics. You will also coach and mentor engineers to help them understand how their work contributes to the broader vision and enables safe and scalable drone delivery operations.

Integrate drone delivery into the DoorDash marketplace. Define how merchant preparation, order readiness, dispatch timing, routing, customer promises, delivery-zone eligibility, and fulfillment decisions interact with aircraft availability, weather, airspace, and operational constraints.

Lead the autonomy product roadmap. Establish priorities across mission planning, autonomous path and motion planning, contingency behaviors, rerouting, detect-and-avoid integration, vehicle health, payload handling, landing and delivery behaviors, and remote assistance.

Define the data strategy for autonomous aviation. Determine which geospatial, terrain, obstacle, weather, airspace, population-risk, connectivity, landing-zone, and operational data layers should be built internally, licensed, sourced through partners, or generated by the fleet.

Build UTM and airspace-management capabilities. Lead product requirements for operational-volume generation, strategic and tactical deconfliction, dynamic rerouting, airspace authorization, constraint management, conformance monitoring, and interoperability with UTM service providers and public airspace systems.

Lead standards compliance and engagement. Productize regulatory compliance. Translate Part 135 operating requirements, BVLOS approvals, safety cases, operational limitations, and emerging Part 108 concepts into reusable software, data, workflow, auditability, and configuration-management capabilities.

Make build, buy, and partner decisions. Evaluate technology providers, data sources, autonomy components, and infrastructure partners based on strategic differentiation, integration complexity, operational risk, economics, and time to market.

As Senior Product Manager for Orchestration, you will own how dbt runs in production: how jobs are scheduled and triggered, how they recover when something goes wrong, and how teams find out and fix it.

You will own the vision, roadmap, and outcomes for orchestration on the dbt platform. That covers the job scheduler, triggers and job chaining, retries and run reliability, concurrency and queueing, jobs as code, run monitoring, and notifications. Data teams of every size depend on these systems every day, from a single nightly job to enterprise deployments with hundreds of interdependent jobs across many projects.

sections.title: What You’ll Do
bullets: Own the orchestration strategy and roadmap

Define and own the vision and roadmap for dbt platform orchestration, including scheduling, event- and API-based triggers, chaining across jobs and projects, retries, concurrency and queueing, and jobs as code. Turn that vision into clear priorities, sequencing, and tradeoffs.
Set success metrics for run reliability, on-time delivery, and time to recovery, and hold yourself accountable for moving them.
Decide where to invest, what to build, and what not to build, using customer evidence, usage data, and technical judgment.
Make production dbt reliable and observable
Partner with engineering to improve run reliability: fewer failed or stuck runs, clearer classification of what went wrong, and faster recovery when it does.
Own notifications and run monitoring across email, Slack, webhooks, and integrations, so teams hear about failures quickly, understand what broke, and know what to do next.
Work with the v2 and dbt State teams to make sure jobs build only what they need to, and stay fast and cost-efficient at scale.

sections.title: About the role
paras: Motive is investing deeply in Connected Devices as the physical backbone of our platform, and Equipment Monitoring is one of the largest growth opportunities in the portfolio. We help customers track, protect, and optimize a vast range of assets — trailers, reefer units, construction equipment, small tools, and cargo — using rugged, purpose-built devices such as the Asset Gateway, Motive Beacon, and Environmental Sensor, alongside partner networks and OEM integrations through the AEMP 2.0 ecosystem.

As Senior / Staff Product Manager, Connected Devices (Equipment Monitoring), you will be t he dedicated product leader for the entire in-field device surface of the Equipment Monitoring line. You will own the hardware and firmware roadmap, drive New Product Introductions from concept through mass production, own the reliability and performance of the devices already deployed, and lead the product side of our device partnerships that extend where and how assets can be found.

This is a role with unusually direct leverage. Equipment Monitoring anchors Motive's multi-product enterprise deals — the quality of these devices shapes not just one line but the credibility of the platform. You will report to the VP of Connected Devices and partner closely with the Equipment Monitoring product team, who own the cloud, workflow, and customer-facing experience. The dividing line is clean: once data leaves the device, it's theirs; everything up to that point is yours.

sections.title: What you'll do
bullets: Own the hardware and firmware roadmap for Equipment Monitoring in-field devices — asset gateways, beacons, environmental and door sensors, power accessories, and the device form factors that don't exist yet.

Drive NPI execution end-to-end from problem definition and sourcing through EVT, DVT, PVT, certification (FCC, PTCRB, carrier approvals, IP ratings, industrial environmental specs), MP ramp, and post-launch stabilization.

Own the installed base. Field failure and RMA rates, battery life as measured in the field rather than on the bench, connectivity and positioning performance, install success — these are your metrics, and improving them is as much the job as shipping the next device.

Define and prioritize firmware features that extend the value of devices already deployed — power optimization, connectivity resilience, positioning accuracy, sensor fusion, OTA reliability and staged rollout, diagnostics, security, and fleet-level observability.

Lead the product side of device partnerships. Motive is extending asset visibility through partner and mesh networks; you will own the technical and product decisions in those programs while BD and Supply Chain own the commercial terms.

Make the hard trade-offs across feature set, BOM cost, power budget, connectivity (cellular, LPWAN, BLE, GNSS), antenna performance, manufacturability, ruggedness, install experience, quality, and schedule — and communicate those decisions clearly across the organization.

Translate customer and market signals into crisp requirements by running discovery across construction, trucking and logistics, agriculture, energy, field service, and food and beverage; synthesizing input from Sales, Support, Install, and Customer Success; and separating one-off requests from generalizable needs.

Write strong PRDs and technical specs that frame the problem, the constraints, and the decisions — and keep Hardware, Firmware, Mechanical, Quality, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, and TPM aligned through every gate.

sections.title: What we're looking for
bullets: 6+ years of product management experience , with meaningful time shipping IoT, telematics, tracking, or connected hardware products from concept through mass production — and sustaining them through post-launch iteration.

Proven ownership of at least one full hardware NPI that reached material volume (ideally 100K+ units), including navigating EVT/DVT/PVT/MP gates, regulatory certifications, and supplier / contract-manufacturer relationships. We will ask you to name it.

Direct experience owning firmware roadmaps , including OTA update strategy and staged rollouts, release trains, device provisioning and security, telemetry design, and observability for devices operating in harsh, bandwidth-constrained, power-constrained environments.

Demonstrated ownership of field reliability — you've been the PM when a deployed product was failing, and you can describe how you found the cause, what you changed, and what the number looked like afterward.
Demonstrated ability to lead ambiguous, cross-functional initiatives and influence roadmaps across engineering, operations, and GTM without direct authority.
Customer empathy paired with data fluency — you run discovery in the real world as comfortably as you pull device telemetry and field-performance data, and use both to prioritize.
Excellent written and verbal communication , with the ability to move fluently between executives, hardware and firmware engineers, cloud engineers, GTM teams, and customers without losing signal.
Trailblazer mindset — humble, kind, curious, and open to learning, with a strong bias to action and a willingness to commit and disagree productively.

Hi, we're Oscar. We're hiring a Staff Product Manager, Virtual Care to join our Product team.

Oscar is the first health insurance company built around a full stack technology platform and a relentless focus on serving our members. We started Oscar in 2012 to create the kind of health insurance company we would want for ourselves—one that behaves like a doctor in the family.

sections.title: About the role:
paras: As a Staff Product Manager, you’ll lead product development for Oscar Virtual Care (OVC), improving how members access care and how clinicians deliver it. Your work will span the experience before, during, and after a visit, from intake and scheduling to clinical documentation, treatment, and follow-up.

Oscar brings together a health plan and its own care delivery organization, creating an opportunity to connect product decisions directly to the cost and quality of care. You’ll work with clinical and business partners to identify where technology can help members get the care they need. This includes improving access to virtual care and health assessments, supporting effective clinical workflows, and reducing administrative work for care teams.
You’ll turn ambiguous problems into a clear product direction, align partners around priorities, and work with engineering, design, and data science to deliver and measure results.

sections.title: Responsibilities:
bullets: Define and execute the product strategy and roadmap for Virtual Care. Prioritize investments based on their expected impact on affordability, clinical outcomes, member experience, and operating efficiency.
Lead discovery with members, clinicians, and operations teams. Combine user research with data analysis to identify problems, challenge assumptions, and build a business case for product investments.

Improve the member journey from finding and accessing care through the visit and follow-up. Reduce friction in intake and scheduling, improve visit completion, and help care teams share context and coordinate next steps.

Build tools that help clinicians deliver high-quality care efficiently, including reviewing medical history, documenting encounters, addressing care gaps, and ordering appropriate tests and treatments. Evaluate opportunities for AI and automation to reduce administrative work while maintaining clinical quality.
Define success metrics and measure the clinical, financial, and operational impact of product changes. Use findings to refine priorities and improve the experience after launch.

Lead alignment across clinical, operations, engineering, design, and data science partners. Bring clear recommendations, work through competing needs and tradeoffs, and establish decisions that move the work forward.

Own complex initiatives from problem definition through delivery. Write clear requirements, manage dependencies and risks, and resolve issues across teams with the autonomy expected of a Senior Product Manager.
Invest in strengthening the talent on Oscar's product team, by developing more junior team members through mentorship.

5+ years of experience in driving rigorous prioritization processes.
5+ years of experience with tech systems and understanding basic technology infrastructure such as backend services, database relationships, and leveraging database tools such as SQL.
3+ years of experience leading complex, cross-domain initiatives.
3+ years of experience root-causing ambiguous problems, building roadmaps towards a solution, and successfully executing against that roadmap.

Siteline is a fast-growing Series A startup transforming how construction companies get paid, headquartered in San Francisco.

Specialty trade contractors build the infrastructure America runs on, from data centers and schools to highways and hospitals. Yet most are still managing millions of dollars in billing and payments through spreadsheets and manual processes.

WHAT PROBLEMS ARE WE SOLVING

Construction is the slowest paid industry, with contractors waiting around 96 days to get paid. For those 96 days, subcontractors are funding payroll, materials, equipment, and the cost of actually doing the work - all before seeing a single payment. It’s little wonder they describe themselves as “America’s largest bank”.

sections.title: ABOUT SITELINE
paras: Our mission is simple: get subcontractors paid faster. And we’re damn good at it. Siteline customers average just 55 days to payment, and that number keeps falling.

We’re building in a massive, underserved market with no true direct competitor. And while AI is reshaping industries everywhere, the physical infrastructure our customers build isn’t going anywhere. Data centers, hospitals, schools, roads, and power infrastructure still have to be built -and the contractors building them need a radically better way to manage their receivables.

sections.title: WHY ARE WE BUILDING THIS?
paras: Construction software has historically been built for General Contractors. We’re building for the subcontractors actually doing the work.
These businesses are managing millions of dollars on spreadsheets, printouts, ERP reports, and a whole lot of manual work to get paid.
Every project has different billing requirements, different deadlines, and different paperwork. Miss something, and payment can get pushed out another 30 days.

smartrecruiters:servicenow:7440001507146.summary: CRM Voice AI builds autonomous voice agents for customer service that resolve customer interactions end-to-end and drive significant value for the business. We're a team inside ServiceNow's CRM business unit, shipping production voice AI with enterprise customers today and scaling aggressively. Our agents run on a real-time streaming pipeline with best-in-class orchestration, integrated into the same platform where many of our customers already manage their front, middle, and back-office workflows. For those that don't, the voice agent is often the tip of the spear that brings them in. We compete directly against well-funded AI startups and CCaaS incumbents, and we're winning.

sections.title: How We Work:
paras: We work in pods - small, dedicated teams embedded with a single enterprise customer, building their voice agents from first call to self-sufficiency. A pod owns the full lifecycle: agent shadowing, conversation design, build, production go-live, monitoring and optimization and the handoff that makes the customer self-sufficient so the pod can move on to the next one. Each pod pairs forward-deployed engineers with a product manager who owns both the customer outcome and the product learning that comes from it.

Every PM on this team runs at least one pod directly and has visibility across others. You're in the customer's world - on their calls, in their systems, solving their problems - while simultaneously shaping what the product becomes. The learnings from your pods feed directly into the platform roadmap and into repeatable, productized assets that scale beyond any single customer.

sections.title: What This Role Owns:
bullets: For those pods, you and your team of FDEs own agent design, the build and evaluation.

sections.title: Why This and Not Somewhere Else:
paras: This role puts you directly in front of enterprise customers running production voice AI from day one. You're not waiting to earn customer exposure - it's the job. The pod model means you'll accumulate more production voice AI experience in a year than most PMs get in several, across different industries, different contact center environments, and different conversation types. At the same time, the evaluation frameworks and agentic design patterns you build have reach well beyond your own pods. This team has a direct seat at the platform table, so the tooling you create shapes how ServiceNow thinks about voice agent quality at scale.

sections.title: What You Bring:
bullets: Experience in leveraging or critically thinking about how to integrate AI into work processes, decision-making, or problem-solving. This may include using AI-powered tools, automating workflows, analyzing AI-driven insights, or exploring AI's potential impact on the function or industry.
5+ years of product management experience, or equivalent experience in a technical role such as engineering, solutions consulting, or technical program management where you owned product outcomes.
Hands-on experience building and evaluating AI agents or conversational AI systems - conversation design, prompt engineering, testing and iteration against real user interactions.
Comfort with data and evaluation. You think naturally about how to measure whether something is working and how to build systems that do it at scale.
Experience working directly with customers or end users on technical products. You don't need enterprise sales experience, but you need to have been in the room where the work happens.
Strong technical foundation. You can read code, understand API contracts, and hold your own with engineers on system design.
An instinct for repeatable process. You see a problem solved once and immediately think about how to solve it for every customer.
Experience with conversational AI, voice technology, or contact center operations.
